title: Dusting desks, shelves and office seating
audience: Cleaners who dust desks, shelves, lamps, seating and small office items.
learningOutcomes: Dust fabric and leather seating from the top down using the right cloth or mitt.
Dust a desk lamp safely and return it to its exact position.
Apply furniture polish only when the client has asked for it, and only with the grain.

instruction.heading: Fabric and leather seating
instruction.body: Dust chairs and sofas with a cloth, a mitt, or a wand. Begin at the upper edge of the back and the arms, and work down to the seat face. Keep strokes in one direction so that the fabric nap wears evenly. Do not press so hard that the surface is marked.

instruction.heading: Desk lamps
instruction.body: A lamp may still be warm from use, so check it before you touch it. Dust from the top down with a cloth or mitt, lift the base to clean underneath, and set the lamp back exactly where it was.

instruction.heading: Desk tops and shelves
instruction.body: Desk tops and shelves are usually solid timber or laminate. Dust the open areas of a desk without moving papers. On shelves, work from the top shelf to the bottom and from the back forward. Remove items only where you must, wipe the shelf, and put each item back in its original place.

instruction.heading: Polish and client requests
instruction.body: Apply furniture polish only when the client has asked for it. Apply it to a cloth rather than directly onto the surface, and wipe along the grain of the wood. Polish left on a surface attracts dust, so use it sparingly.

procedure: Dust seating from the top downward, keeping strokes in one direction.
Check that the lamp is cool, dust it from the top, and lift the base to clean underneath.
Dust the open areas of desks without moving papers.
Dust shelves starting high and moving down, working from the back forward, and return every item.
Apply polish only if requested, to a cloth, with the grain.

workedExamples.situation: A client has asked for shiny desks. A cleaner polishes the whole surface, including the area under a computer.
workedExamples.reasoning: Polish is applied only where the client asked for it and only with a product suited to the surface. Confirm the request, test a small hidden area first, and keep polish off electronic equipment and the area beneath it. Apply it to a cloth, wipe along the grain, and remove the excess.

equipmentAndPpe: Dusting tools: a cloth, a mitt, or a wand
Cotton cloth and furniture polish, if requested

commonErrors.error: Moving papers while dusting a desk top.
commonErrors.prevention: Dust around papers and leave them in place.

commonErrors.error: Polishing without a request from the client.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the request before any polish is used.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a lamp moved after dusting.
commonErrors.prevention: Return the lamp to its position straight after dusting it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not work on a lamp that is still warm.
Read the label and the safety data sheet for any polish before use, as some products irritate skin or eyes.

qualityStandard: Furniture is dusted from the top downward.
Items are back in their original positions.
No polish residue remains on any surface.
documentationEvidence: Polish use recorded on the job sheet, if applied.
summary: Dust seating and lamps from the top down; check a lamp is cool first.
Leave papers in place and return every item to its position.
Apply polish only on request, to a cloth, and along the grain.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why avoid moving papers while dusting a desk top?
options: It keeps the client's papers in order and avoids disputes
Paper is dusted last, after the frame and drawers
Papers make the desk heavier and they are hard to move back

knowledgeChecks.question: A desk lamp may still be warm. What should you do first?
options: Pour water over it to cool it
Check it is cool before touching it
Dust it with a wet cloth at once

knowledgeChecks.question: When should furniture polish be applied?
options: On every surface at every visit
Only when the client has asked for it
